requirement: Safety-relevant CAN frames shall carry a CRC-8/SAE-J1850 over (Data ID, payload) and a 4-bit alive counter.
The receiver shall reject frames with CRC error, repeated counter, or counter jump larger than max_delta, and shall not refresh reception age on rejected frames.
The receiver shall declare reception timeout when no valid frame has arrived for longer than the configured timeout (EVSE: 250 ms).
CAN pack/unpack code shall be generated from the DBC; C and Python codecs shall agree bit-for-bit and round-trip physical values within one LSB.
The scheduler shall release each task exactly at its declared period and offset on the 1 ms tick.
The scheduler shall record per-task maximum execution time and count budget overruns.
Alive supervision shall detect a periodic task that fails to report its checkpoint for 2 consecutive 100 ms supervision cycles and shall command SAFE_STOP.
The torque monitor shall cut all motor torque when the sum of commanded wheel torques exceeds the pedal-derived envelope plus 10 % of maximum for 50 ms (fault-tolerant time interval <= 100 ms).
The safe-state manager shall never de-escalate within an operation cycle.
Qualified faults shall be stored as confirmed DTCs with UDS status bits, occurrence counter and freeze-frame data.
If |APPS1 - APPS2| > 10 % or either track is out of range for more than 100 ms, the APPS fault shall latch and no positive propulsion torque shall be requested.
If the brake is applied while pedal > 25 %, propulsion torque shall be removed until pedal < 5 % (brake-throttle override).
Total motor torque shall not exceed the torque derived from the BMS discharge (charge) current limit and pack voltage.
On pedal lift-off, regenerative torque shall decelerate the vehicle at up to 1.5 m/s^2, fading to zero below 2 m/s.
On a mu = 0.3 surface at full pedal, traction control shall keep mean driven-wheel slip <= 0.25 after the first 0.5 s.
Torque vectoring shall reduce RMS yaw-rate tracking error during a step-steer manoeuvre by >= 30 % versus TV disabled.
Torque vectoring shall redistribute torque left/right without changing the total requested torque.
The SOC EKF shall converge to within 3 % of true SOC within 600 s from a 20 % initial error.
A cell voltage above 4.22 V for 100 ms shall raise a SEVERE fault: current limits to zero, then contactors open.
A cell voltage above 4.30 V shall open the contactors within 50 ms without waiting for current decay.
A cell temperature above 60 degC for 1 s shall raise a SEVERE fault.
An implausible cell-voltage or temperature reading shall raise a SEVERE fault.
The main positive contactor shall close only after DC-link voltage reaches 95 % of pack voltage; precharge not completing within 1 s shall latch a fault with all contactors open.
DC-link voltage already near pack voltage at precharge start shall be diagnosed as a welded main contactor.
Charge and discharge current limits shall derate with temperature, SOC and the cell-voltage window, reaching zero at the limits.
Passive balancing shall bleed cells above vmin + 10 mV only at low current or while charging and only when spread > 15 mV.
DC contactors shall close only after cable check passed, HV is closed, and |EVSE voltage - pack voltage| < 20 V.
Requested charge current shall not exceed min(BMS charge limit, EVSE maximum current).
The CV loop shall keep the maximum cell voltage <= 4.20 V throughout a fast charge.
Loss of EVSE communication shall abort the session: current request zero and DC contactors open within 300 ms of the last valid frame.
Unplug or EVSE emergency stop shall abort the session within 50 ms.
At target SOC the session shall ramp current down and open contactors only after EVSE current < 2 A (or 2 s timeout).
A 10 % to 80 % DC fast charge from 25 degC shall complete in under 40 minutes with cell temperature below 50 degC.
Battery cooling shall engage above 35 degC when driving and above 32 degC during DC fast charge.
PID controllers shall use anti-windup so that the integrator stays bounded under sustained saturation.
During a DC fast charge session the pack shall be heated when tmin < 20 degC (preconditioning).
Direction indicators shall flash at 90 +/- 30 flashes/min with ~50 % duty, first flash on activation.
Hazard warning shall take priority over direction indication.
A short stalk tap (< 400 ms) shall produce exactly 3 flashes (lane-change).
Regenerative braking shall light the stop lamps above 1.3 m/s^2 and shall not light them below 0.7 m/s^2.
Deceleration >= 6 m/s^2 above 50 km/h shall flash the stop lamps at 4 Hz (ESS); after stopping, hazards shall activate automatically.
Automatic headlamps shall switch on within 2 s of ambient illumination below 1000 lux.
A crash signal shall unlock all doors and activate hazard warning.
Doors shall auto-lock above 8 km/h.
During power-window closing, force on an obstruction in the 4-200 mm zone shall stay below 100 N and the window shall reverse.
One-touch auto-up shall close the window fully without a held switch.
